title: The Western Front
subject: History
unit: Spring 1: Challenges for Britain, Europe and the wider world: the First World War
source: Written for history/y9 lesson 3 (Western Front map (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 3. Draw the front line from the Channel coast to Switzerland using the slides, and label the battles.

blocks.caption: Outline from Natural Earth (public domain); modern coastlines and borders.

questions.q: Describe three hardships of trench life.
questions.a: For example: mud and cold, rats and lice, constant danger of shells and snipers
questions.model: Think of the body, the place and the danger. Body: trench foot. Place: mud, rats, lice. Danger: shells and snipers. Three hardships.

questions.q: Why were trenches dug in a zigzag?
questions.a: To stop blasts and attackers travelling along the trench
Mental injury was not well understood; some thought it was cowardice

questions.q: Core: Draw a labelled bird's-eye diagram of a trench system with six features and one fact about each.
questions.a: Front, support, reserve and communication trenches, barbed wire, No Man's Land, each with a fact
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: a zigzag line labelled 'front-line trench: soldiers on watch', with barbed wire in front.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box: 'What was the hardest part of trench life?' Give a reasoned answer.
questions.a: Reasoned answer, for example constant fear of shelling, linked to shell shock

questions.q: Stretch: How did the Somme change how people at home saw the war?
questions.a: Huge losses, including whole Pals battalions from one town, shocked people and ended hopes of a quick victory

questions.q: The Battle of the Somme began on:
Big question: what was the hardest part of life on the Western Front?
questions.a: Reasoned answer: mud, disease, boredom, fear and the mental strain that caused shell shock
